article.title: the case for dismantling the israeli state
article.author: Socialist Forum
article.content: Over 680,000 Palestinians have been killed by Israel’s machinery of mass slaughter since the start of October 2023. According to UN Raconteur Francesca Albanese, 380,000 of those murdered in Gaza have been infants under the age of five. Nearly thirty years ago, Edward Said said that the situation between Israel and Palestine had reached a “bloody impasse”, and called for a dissolution of Zionist Israel into one unified secular Palestinian state. In his New York Times essay, entitled “ One-State Solution ”, Said stated, “I see no other way than to begin now to speak about sharing the land that has thrust us together, sharing it in a truly democratic way, with equal rights for each citizen.” Palestinians have long called for the ending of the settler colonial regime of Israel, having already endured several decades of Israel’s war on their sense of dignity and livelihoods and the constant stealing of more and more land. “Israeli and Zionist militias have been massacring Palestinians for approximately a hundred years now,” said the scholar Refaat Alareer, adding, “Israel is not satisfied with anything but total victory for its colonial rule (146). Alareer was murdered along with members of his family by Israeli drones in late 2023. There can be no freedom and dignity or even equality for Palestinians unless Israel as it is politically and materially constituted is no more. Until then, the core of Israeli life, which is the same core that has driven much of European colonialism, shall carry on, destroying the land and its indigenous cultures for decades onwards. This is a pivotal moment in world history. The U.S. left, including our left-leaning electeds, indeed all socialists, must move beyond repeated calls for ceasefires and peace talks. Instead we must forthrightly call for the end of Israel as a political entity, and for a free and liberated Palestine in its stead. Otherwise, the Palestinian people will be exterminated and in a few decades time, the liberals among us will lead chants of “honoring” the land at the very same spots where actual Palestinians had once lived. Concurrently, the expansion of a Greater Israel and its plans for eliminating an independent Palestine that could challenge its social and political order does put our own attempts at developing a truly socialist project in America at grave risk. We’ve already seen the American Zionist Committee for Public Affairs (AIPAC) pouring tens of millions of U.S.dollars into our own national and local elections, propping up far-right candidates like a Steve Scalise, whose main claim to infamy was having attended a white supremacist conference that was co-founded by the Klansman and former gubernatorial candidate David Duke. Clearly, what matters to AIPAC is maintaining a coalition of anti-socialist anti-progressive elements that shall promise an endless supply of guns to the Zionist state. Conversely, those elected like Scalise want an American empire to thrive forever, a regime that relies so heavily on easy access to oil and raw minerals abroad, especially in the same Western Asian region that Israel hopes to conquer. In this article, we will be arguing for a complete end of the political entity known as Israel. No more two states. No more meaningless ceasefires that only serve the Israeli state in buying time to kill ever more innocent Palestinians or to encroach on more Palestinian land. We believe that the continued existence of Israel will mean a rabid and powerful co-partner in sustaining a global American empire, the destruction of Palestine and its thousands of years of culture and civilization. Moreover, it helps ensure the elevation of anti-socialist and pro-regressive domestic politics within the formal bounds of the U.S. That, in turn, would sink any attempts at bringing forth critical and humane policies for the U.S. working class, including those of Arab and Palestinian descent. Our fates are tied. Legal scholar Noura Erakat put the situation well in her statement to the U.N. on the matter of Israel’s genocide and how it serves the U.S. empire, and thereby threatens world peace, “Do not sit in the seat of power and do nothing. The United States is an empire but the United States is not the world. You are the world- each and every one of you has the capacity to halt this charade and to fulfill the minimal mandate of protecting a people’s right to exist.” Attaining a free and unified Palestine in place of settler colonial Israel, against the tide of reaction, must remain a primary issue, not secondary, for our movements, and for those claiming to represent us in the halls of Congress. Otherwise, its defeat shall haunt us in the Western left for centuries to come. there is no american hegemony without israel Israel has always been a colonialist entity, and a critical node in European, and later, American imperial designs globally. Its Zionist forefather, the Austrian Theodore Herzl , openly claimed the movement as being deeply intertwined with so-called expansionism of “Western” civilization, going so far as penning letters of allegiance to the British Empire during its brutal repression and takeover of Africa in the mid-to-late 1800s. The Nakba wasn’t just a continuation of European colonization and genocide of Indigenous peoples of the Americas. The Israeli state also collaborated with various Western interests, inspired by Herzl’s lessons and insights, on how to achieve statehood through mass killing and obscuring of history. It was Israel, after all, that swiftly colluded militarily with British and French forces in the occupation of the Suez Canal against the sovereign interests of the Nasser-led Egyptian government. After the ‘67 war, Israel had proven itself to the U.S. political establishment, thus becoming a closer ally and a critical node for U.S. proxy wars throughout the region and even beyond. In 1976, Israel’s government, under what would be described now, at least in comparison to Bibi, as “moderate” leadership, welcomed John Vorster , the Prime Minister of apartheid South Africa. That same year, the explicitly white supremacist government in South Africa had massacred nearly 700 Africans, nearly all of them students protesting against white rule (some victims were less than 12 years old).. Vorster too, like much of the South African white Dutch leadership, either were Nazis during WWII or were deeply sympathetic. In the midst of this political landscape of brutality and Dutch colonization, fittingly, the Israeli PM, Yitzhak Rabin, praised Vorster and his regime as a “force for freedom” and Israel became a stalwart ally of South Africa – one of the few nations to adopt that position. Israel’s government, after all, was willing to sell the white minority government nuclear weapons. Israel forged a strategic military and political relationship with the Afrikaner-led government, violating international rules and sanctions. An investigation by Open Secrets in 2017 revealed more details about the long-standing, close relationship between Tel Aviv and Pretoria—an alliance that strengthened in the 1970s when the two countries clandestinely traded weapons. These activities amounted to sanctions-busting in a period where the United Nations (UN) had placed a compulsory arms embargo on apartheid South Africa. Declassified South African Department of Defence documents revealed that by 1975 South African state-owned weapons company Armscor officials set up a permanent office in Tel Aviv, allowing the South Africans to bust sanctions under the cover of diplomacy. Such alliances allowed the white supremacist regime in South Africa to lengthen the country’s lifespan by providing weaponry and support that emboldened South Africa to routinely invade neighboring African nations, including several years of South African white occupation of what would become the nation of Namibia. The Israeli-Afrikaner relationship also exemplifies how willing and capable Israel has been, even under moderate leadership, to strengthen other elements of American global dominance. Through South Africa, the U.S. had its own anti-communist anti-African independence weapon that it sought to aim and direct at Namibia, Angola, and the ANC. Israel played its role in this mission, risking the sanctity of African soil and true nationalism. Today, Israel plays that same role, helping to support American-backed regimes in as far away as Latin America. Itay Mack at +972 Magazine summarizes , At a recent meeting of the Knesset’s Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, representatives of Israel’s Foreign Ministry complained of the hardships they face in democratic countries in Latin America, and the success of “Palestinian diplomatic terrorism” in those states. In comparison, the Israeli diplomats pointed with great pride to the close relations with the regime in Honduras, a country that had a military coup in 2009, which is undergoing a process of militarization, and whose security forces are known to assassinate human rights activists, workers’ rights activists, and those fighting for indigenous rights. Modi’s India, which has been promoted as an antidote to alleged Chinese dominance in Asia, has also been a direct beneficiary of Israeli military and surveillance support. Kashmir, yet another Muslim-majority region, remains occupied by Indian forces thanks in large part to the selling and distribution of Israeli drones and other kinds of military equipment. With now the world’s fourth largest weapons manufacturing and war manufacturing industry, Israel does its part in feeding weapons between U.S.-aligned nations, sometimes at the behest of American global interests. Indeed, Israel’s government, first under the Labour Party, and now under Likud, has routinely collaborated with major industries that are pro-Western and pro-U.S.; the best example is oil. Prior to 1979 and the birth of the Iranian Revolution, Iran was dominated by the Shah Pahlavi dynasty that was put in place through a C.I.A coup. A significant portion of its oil wealth was subsequently funneled into the coffers of private Western companies such as BP. While this was happening, Israel aided the Shah regime in its repression of the Iranian people. The oil sector strengthened America’s position as a worldwide force for capitalist expansion and power. The recent U.S.-Israeli war on Iran is similar. The intention is to weaken the existing Iranian government and take over Iran’s oil reserves through Western-backed companies. Trump literally said the quiet part out loud about this joint venture when attacking Iran, stating that the U.S. goal was “to take the oil” from Iran. Israel is assisting in that process. As we’ve seen with Venezuela after the capture of Maduro and his wife, Flores, once socialist or nationalist regimes fall, and their resources are up for grabs, they flow directly into pro-Western industries, thereby strengthening their economic and political positions inside the U.S. as well as broad. Until the recent genocide, Saudi Arabia, an epicenter of oil and Western interests, had begun to normalize relations with Israel and Israel, in turn, has worked covertly to assist its regime. Even though elements of the Saudi regime have stood firm on wanting an independent Palestine state, its ruler, Mohammed bin Salman (MBS), has expressed a far more ruthless, and more honest, appraisal of the Palestinian cause for statehood. Journalist Karen Elliot writes , “‘He [MBS] has this vision of Israel and Saudi Arabia as the two big powers [in the region] working hand in hand. It won’t be easy until there’s some resolution in Gaza, but Saudis who know him well will tell you he can’t allow Saudi interests to be forever retarded by the Palestinians.’” Finally, one cannot forget the immense amount of real estate and private developer power that would sweep through Gaza and the rest of the West Bank if Isreel is allowed to persist in its campaign of genocide and disposession. Once again, oil, retail and real estate form a global bloc pact that often stands against even the most moderate of social democratic reforms. As Israel morphs into Greater Israel, consuming large swaths of Lebanon and Syria, the U.S. system sees its own array of colonial and capitalistic interests expand in power and influence. As U.S. real estate plows through the beaches of Gaza City, Palestinians are forced to either comply or be extinguished. Global real estate and oil markets cheer, as they too gain an upper hand in influencing and shaping politics across the globe including within the U.S., pouring money into politicians and agendas that can only be described as fascist. The U.S.-Israeli influence at the domestic level While Israel strengthens facism internationally, it also reinforces America’s position as a global hegemon and directly impacts U.S. politics in a highly corrosive manner. During the hotly contested 2024 congressional election that pitted left-leaning congress members against so-called centrists from within the Democratic party, AIPAC, Israel’s most powerful lobby, poured a whopping $8.5 million alone into the campaign coffers of Wesley Bell, the main center-right candidate seeking to unseat Cori Bush, a leading member of the progressive “Squad” inside Congress. This money allowed Bell, someone without any organic grassroots support, to hire support staff and to establish a presence in the district that Bush had already represented in the St. Louis area. This resulted in Bush’s defeat by Bell in 2024 who, to this day, routinely expresses ardent support for Zionism, despite Israel’s genocide. With the backing of AIPAC, Bell, a conservative figure who is against policies like Medicare-for-All and measures to make law enforcement accountable, which were core issues for Cori Bush’s short time in office, has managed to keep himself in power. From a recent NBC report covering the primary race between Bush and Bell: In total, Bell’s campaign and outside allies outspent Bush by a staggering 27-to-1 ratio, according to AdImpact, an ad-tracking service. United Democracy Project — the super PAC linked to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, the pro-Israel advocacy group known as AIPAC — spent $2 million to support Bell, largely through negative ads attacking Bush. One such ad slammed Bush for being critical of former Vice President Kamala Harris. Bush herself was not a radical political figure, certainly not someone who’d be described as a Marxist. Yet she’d been targeted by Zionist-aligned forces, simply because she raised her voice on Palestine and for this, she’s been kept out of Congress, while medical bills for most Americans have continued to rise, and basic costs of living are sinking the rest of us. The prototypical AIPAC candidate is pro-war pro-genocide very much of the status quo when it comes to basic social democratic policies that would at least benefit a broader section of our own working class. This was on display in the Michigan primary race for U.S. senate between Abdul El-Sayed and Haley Stevens. El-Sayed is a strong proponent, himself a medical professional, of Medicare-for-All as a basic public policy. Stevens is not. She’s gone so far as to “ walk back” from endorsing Medicare-for-All while she was serving as congressperson. Stevens received the backing of AIPAC in her race against El-Sayed, who otherwise is a fairly moderate candidate. But since El-Sayed criticizes the state of Israel and its unending list of crimes against the Palestinian people, he’s been targeted for defeat. Over the past several years alone, AIPAC has been a leading spender in local and national races throughout the country. Even the New York Times , not exactly known for their hard-hitting anti-imperialist news, stated , In less than five years, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee has become one of the biggest spenders in American elections, flooding the airwaves in congressional races across the country. Since its first involvement in elections, the amount of money AIPAC-affiliated political action committees have spent on campaign advertising and outreach to voters has more than doubled, from $29.3 million to $67.2 million, with much of it spent in Democratic primaries. Zionists are securely part of the grand antisocialist antiprogressive coalition inside the U.S., as it leans on sections of civil society that support them in return for their support for colonization and extraction of resources from the rest of West Asia. Thus, whatever the oil industry prefers or what healthcare executives want in terms of pushing the Democratic party and the Republicans further and further away from even social democratic, moderate reforms, AIPAC and its Zionist allies will pursue those same agendas broadly: their interests are already intertwined as it relates to the exploitation of other peoples’ resources, including labor; and Israel will not survive a truly revolutionary socialist state takeover, or even, for that matter, a moderate one in which aid to Israel would be cut. Not to mention the coalitions they’ve made are the very same forces who otherwise do not desire a socialist world, not even a social democratic one. As Sam Judy at the Dallas Weekly put it : “Likewise, oil companies and military defense corporations have a direct stake in both violence against and the displacement of Palestinians.” Our American industry of warmaking has benefited from Israel’s genocide and its insistence on being a fascist militarized state. Essentially, killing of Palestinians has been “good” business for the U.S. defense industry for the last several decades alone. Not to mention the innumerable American corporations that operate within Israel, selling their goods and services to a people desperate to be seen as part of the “West”’s consumer market. From the Council of Foreign Relations , Israel has been the largest cumulative recipient of U.S. foreign aid since its founding, receiving over $300 billion (adjusted for inflation) in total economic and military assistance. While the United States has also provided large foreign aid packages to other Middle Eastern countries, particularly Egypt and Iraq, Israel stands apart. Conversely, the U.S. capitalist and colonialist order, itself shaped by generations of Euro-settler genocide against Indigenous peoples, has sought to placate Zionist interests so that this alliance can thrive. This means having our immigration system seek out and target international students, many of them Arab or at least Muslim, who’ve spoken truth about Israel’s campaign of extermination. Freedom of speech is being actively curtailed for the sake of maintaining this sordid but perhaps unsurprising alliance between colonialists in the U.S., and those inside Israel. Mahmoud Khalil is one of the more well-known examples of this, sought out and detained for his own moderate stances on Palestine and Israel. Although a legal permanent resident, Khalil had been kidnapped by immigration officials for his refusal to accept Israeli genocide. But there have been countless others who’ve been either detained or somehow punished for their stance against Palestinian extermination. From the Intercept : “Since the beginning of Israel’s war on Gaza, academics in fields including politics, sociology, Japanese literature , public health, Latin American and Caribbean studies, Middle East and African studies, mathematics, education, and more have been fired, suspended, or removed from the classroom for pro-Palestine, anti-Israel speech.” Rumeysa Ozturk, a Turkish student at Tufts, was initially “swarmed” with ICE agents and disappeared for the apparent criminal act of penning a pro-Palestinian op-ed. “ I am choosing to return home as planned to continue my career as a woman scholar without losing more time to the state-imposed violence and hostility I have experienced in the United States — all for nothing more than co-signing an op-ed advocating for Palestinian rights ,” Ozturk announced after finally being released from detention. For an entire year, Leqaa Kordia was kept in an ICE detention facility in Texas, far away from her home and community in New Jersey. Kordia herself has been pro-Palestinian and for that humane position, she was forced to endure brutal health conditions, including a seizure. In a letter shared by her lawyers, she recounted, “For three days in the emergency room, my hands and legs were weighed down by heavy chains.” Instead of being treated as a human being, she was purposefully abused all because she and others like her refuse to bow down to settler colonialist oppression and repression. America’s prime business is war and extraction of resources from across the world with which Israel is completely aligned. To preserve this bond between them, measures are taken politically to not just make Zionism an accepted truth by all in Western Asia but also within the mainstream civil and political corridors of U.S. life. We’ve slowly become one nation under Christian fascism, Zionism, and white supremacist mythology. This coming together is now being formally sealed through the “2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)”. As reported by Ben Freeman, Section 224 lays the groundwork for bilateral research and development, co-production of weapons, joint ventures, licensing agreements, and seemingly every manner of U.S.-Israeli military-industrial complex cooperation. The U.S. and Israel already work together heavily on missile defense, but this provision would greatly expand coordination to seemingly every area of defense tech, including AI, quantum, autonomous systems, directed energy, cyber, biotech, and many more. It also proposes “network integration” and “data fusion.” In other words, the U.S. military’s data could soon be the Israeli military’s data. Through such policies, the capitalist and colonialist class of the U.S. and the colonialists of Israel are forever striving for one totally united front against the left, against working people, against the colonized. Fascists on either side of the ocean find meaning and momentum in each other, and thus, the Palestinians and the oppressed and working class of even those of us within the imperial core pay a price for their sycophancy. Palestinians themselves have been cognizant of this lethal dynamic for generations since the Nakba of ‘48. Scholar and legendary author of modern Palestinian literature, Ghassan Kanafani, stated , “The Palestinian cause is not a cause for Palestinians only, but a cause for every revolutionary, wherever he is, as a cause of the exploited and oppressed masses in our era.” Kanafani believed this fervently until he was assassinated, along with his 17 year old niece, in an Israeli orchestrated car bomb attack in 1972, having served his people with bravery and cutting insights that threatened the Zionist and U.S. imperialist social order. Many in the Palestinian diaspora, especially those most intimate with Israeli and U.S. violence, who’ve weathered the storms of colonialism, have long recognized our common links across oceans as survivors of American imperialism, of war, of capitalism, of death and the real replacement of indigenous populations by Europeans. Kanafani and others like him long ago warned that our fates are tied. israel wants the extermination of palestine It was only in February of this year when Israeli Finance Minister Ben Smotrich stated in now quintessential Zionist and imperialist arrogance and bloodthirstiness interpreted by the Western press as bravery, what he sees as the new order: “In the end, Israel will occupy the Gaza Strip, implement a military government and establish Jewish settlements there,” adding, “It is impossible to run away from that because it is the truth.” Currently, with a so-called ceasefire in place, Israel remains in military control of at least 70 percent of Gaza. Israeli Prime Minister and war criminal standout Benjamin Netanyahu has spoken of “voluntary emigration” for Palestinians from Gaza. Israeli Defense Minister Israel (yes, that’s his name) Katz and Bibi have been linked to statements and plans to first move Palestinians, much like what was done here during the Trail of Tears in 1830s America, into compounds in Rafah and from there, Palestinians would be “encouraged” to leave the strip entirely. “Netanyahu and Katz have widespread support for what they are planning: 82 percent of Israeli Jews support the expulsion of Palestinians from Gaza,” writes human rights lawyer Zaha Hasssan, “With Israeli elections only weeks away, the overwhelming sentiment among voters cannot be discounted.” The overall goal, it would seem, is to transform Palestine into a real estate bonanza for outside forces, as mentioned earlier. Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, serves on the recently established “Board of Peace”, a grouping of outside entities whose chief purpose is to colonize Gaza’s resources, removing its people out of the way of “ progress.” From Cleveland-Stout at Responsible Statecraft , In fact, Kushner and other board members have advertised the investment opportunities in Gaza’s redevelopment. At the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, Kushner unveiled a $30 billion “master plan” to replace historic sites and landmarks with data centers, industrial zones, residential towers, and seaside resorts. The president’s son-in-law went on to claim that Gaza’s redevelopment will offer “amazing investment opportunities” to the private sector. A report from the UN has bluntly concluded that Israeli forces are seeking to establish “ permanent control over the Gaza Strip while ensuring a Jewish majority in the occupied West Bank and inside Israel.” In 1970, Kanafani, in a now iconic interview with the Australian Broadcasting Company, had defined the Israeli government as a fascist one. Even earlier, he’d pinned Israel as nothing more than an “aggressive expansionist racial structure” which was seeking to mobilize its nationals to “prevent u s from regaining our land, our freedom and our rights.” The goal of Israel has been to eradicate and eliminate Palestinian ownership and claim to the land, replacing the native inhabitants with mainly Europeans and others allied to the cause of Zionist supremacy. Again Kanafani: “It is a colonialist situation.” This is not a disagreement between groups of people who “misunderstand” one another. It is the same blood soaked decision making and patterning that cast a long shadow of European domination, specifically Anglo-American, over the various nations and tribes that had lived on the North American continent for thousands of years, without disease, without major strife. “There was no such thing as Palestinians,” said Golda Meir, the former Israeli prime minister in 1969, using the very same rhetoric that one expects from European colonizers when they first arrived to the U.S., seeing all this land for the taking, impassioned to say that the people who’d lived there for generations were either “impediments” to “progress” or are as real as the flora and fauna. “I don’t go so far as to think that the only good Indian is the dead Indian,” said Theodore Roosevelt in 1886 when America’s empire was rapidly expanding overseas, “but I believe nine out of every ten are, and I shouldn’t like to inquire too closely into the case of the tenth. The most vicious cowboy has more moral principle than the average Indian.” Israel’s conduct during various “moderate” regimes and now under a far more explicitly extremist one will only end in more mass slaughter of the Palestinian people in the same manner by which entire nations of native people across North America had been eliminated by hordes of Euro-Americans. This is a pivotal moment in Palestinian and world history. There is no reformation of an Israeli state that has internally displaced 90 percent of Gaza’s 2.1 million residents, and has left 17,000 children in Gaza without either of their parents. “These children are living in tragic conditions, with many forced to take refuge in torn tents or destroyed homes, in a near-total absence of social care and psychological support.” Whatever aid is being allowed to trickle in has been deliberately used as a method of target practice for the Israelis. “ Witnesses and health workers say Israeli forces have killed hundreds by opening fire on Palestinians trying to reach those food distribution hubs or while crowding around entering aid trucks.” Whether under the guise of “moderation” or “peace”, the Israeli state has always conducted itself with the sole aim of conquering Palestinian land, and of routinely keeping Palestinians in their so-called place. “Mowing the grass” was the common phrase used by Israeli military officials when conducting military strikes every few years inside the Gaza strip, killing Palestinians at a rapid pace. This routine slaughter of Palestinians will survive into a new governing coalition, even if that coalition does not include Bibi Netanyahu. As reported by The Cradle , Netayahu’s election rival for this upcoming Israeli elections himself is viewed as a moderate only because they do not use the same level of genocidal rhetoric at all times. Gadi Eisenkot, who could become Israel’s next prime minister, “served in Netanyahu’s war cabinet during the first months of the Gaza assault and is closely associated with the “Dahiyeh doctrine” of overwhelming force developed during his military career. His differences with Netanyahu concern strategy, responsibility, and the management of war more than any rupture with Zionist policy toward Palestinians or the wider region.” Dr Saad Nimr, professor of political science, described this race as “a competition between the right and the right.” Naftali Bennett, prime minister of Israel who too has become part of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, has voiced opposition to any chances at a Palestinian state. “I haven’t changed. I am a man of the right. I am against a Palestinian state, against giving away territory. I’m a security man,” are his exact words from this summer after nearly three years of a genocidal war against the Palestinian indigenous peoples of the land. With friends like these, who needs enemies. Rightwing or far right, the very existence of Israel itself is a crime against the Palestinian peoples. Its formation is a direct product of Palestinian people having been expelled from their homes in ‘47 and 1948. “We must expel Arabs and take their places…and, if we have to use force… then we have force at our disposal,” were the words of David Ben-Gurion, the father of the bastardized state of Israel, whose Zionist paramilitary forces had participated in the expulsion and killing of Palestinians to make way for Zionist occupation. Between 750,000 to 1 million Palestinians were driven from their homes in Palestine in the formation of Israel nearly 78 years ago, with a majority of them being forced to flee into Gaza where they’ve been since. Israel, for all its attempts at projecting a diverse civil society of occasional Arab and Israeli friendship, sits upon stolen land and bones of Palestinians. Said said “that the very quarters of the city in which I was born, lived and felt at home were taken over by Polish, German, and American immigrants who conquered the city and have made it the unique symbol of their sovereignty, with no place for Palestinian life.” Past and present horrors have merged from the Nakba of ‘48 to now steps being taken by the Israeli establishment for a Final Solution to the Palestinian question. There is no normal nor is there any future whereby an Israeli state should be allowed to function as it has for the past 78 years with near impunity. Unless the Palestinians are truly supported and their claims to their land are honored materially, they will be exterminated. Either Israel is dismantled, or, the Palestinian peoples will become a forever diaspora. A free & united palestine In an interview with Electronic Intifada , Refaat Alareer stated with his usual humor and passion, “I’m an academic; probably the toughest thing I have at home is an expo marker. But if the Israelis go door-to-door to massacre us, I’m going to use that marker to throw it at the soldiers, even if that is the last thing I would be able to do.” Resistance, both militarily and non-violently, have been at the core at Palestinian life, having been compelled to defend themselves against the indomitable might of American imperial hubris and Zionism. Armed Israeli tanks might sometimes hover in one’s imaginations, considering how easily they take up physical space in Palestinian life along with IDF soldiers conducting TikTok dances after committing yet another war crime. Still, Palestinians persist in the face of it, for generations now and they’re never giving up. Said, proudly, said, “ In this, I am confident in saying, we have proved the wrongness of Israel’s policy: there is no getting away from the fact that, as an idea, a memory, and as an often buried or invisible reality, Palestine and its people have simply not disappeared.” As Frantz Fanon once wrote as well, for the native or the indigenous resister, it is always the land that remains most important, maintaining it in some way. So long as Palestinians remain in some ownership of existing land, even parcels of it, the resistance and dream will never be completely abstract. That said, the timeline is swiftly dwindling. Again, the goal for elected socialist and progressive leaders, and for our progressive and leftwing movements inside the U.S. is to see this reality, to see how Palestinians continue to wage struggle against Israel and the Americans, and how we must support them in that struggle for life and at this moment, survival. At the end of it all, the progressive and socialist leader, whether an elected member of Congress or someone who organizes in a labor union, must advocate for a total displacement of what is Israel to make way for a free, independent and a united Palestine (meaning: for Israel proper to become Palestine along with all parts of Gaza and the West Bank). This is required for the above three reasons which we’ve discussed, which include Israel’s complicity in American world domination, Israel’s toxic influence in our domestic politics, and most importantly, the fact that Israel will always be seeking the extermination of the Palestinian peoples and their chances at statehood. For this to be made literal, movement leaders and forces that are part of the U.S. left must advocate for a total embargo of Israel, for all of Netanyahu’s cabinet (himself included) and past Israeli leaders to be arrested and tried, and push for a future Palestinian state whereby rights are no longer attached to one’s faith. Instead, there must be a future state by which equality under the law is made real. No more military courts for Palestinians. All Palestinians to be released from Israeli captivity. Said once more : “In a modern state, all its members are citizens by virtue of their presence and the sharing of rights and responsibilities. Citizenship therefore entitles an Israeli Jew and a Palestinian Arab to the same privileges and resources.” But for this to be something truly meaningful for the ones historically oppressed in the context of Zionist exploitation and colonialism, land must be returned to its original inhabitants. As stated in the previous section, much of Gaza’s current-day residents are those who originally were forced to flee the Nakba of ‘48. For many, they carry their family’s original keys with them to where their homes had once been. In many such cases, homes were simply appropriated by Europeans who’d later on call themselves Israeli and attribute an indigeneity to themselves that does not exist. Nevertheless, returning land is critical if there is to be real justice for a majority of Palestinians. Otherwise, what has happened in post-apartheid South Africa to Africans there will simply be repeated among the Palestinians even in a state that’s supposedly formally independent. Sari Bashi, a former program director at Humans Rights Watch , contextualizes this need for Palestinians:, Given the staggering physical, social and economic destruction that the Israeli military has wreaked on Gaza, the obstruction of humanitarian aid and the likelihood of continued hostilities even if the parties reach a cease-fire, many Palestinians in Gaza will want to relocate away from the strip, at least temporarily. But they have a legal right to return to Gaza, now or in the future. And under international law, the 1948 refugees and their descendants in Gaza, totaling 1.6 million people, also have a right to resettle on the land taken from them and their families three-quarters of a century ago, and to benefit from the housing, infrastructure, services, schools and universities in the land that is now Israel that they have been unlawfully denied. Leila Shomali and Lara Kilani write in Ebb magazine that there is no use of equal rights if there’s no material restitutions made for the original sin of stolen land and in that same process, stolen life. There is no moral legitimacy in the suggestion that these settlers have a ‘right’ to live on stolen Palestinian land, the theft maintained by force, as long as there has been no restoration of Palestinians’ rights. No theories of justice exist in mainstream ethical or philosophical discourse that advocate for a person who has stolen something to rightfully keep what they have taken. The act of theft, by definition, violates the basic principles of theories of justice, which emphasise fairness, equitable distribution of resources, and respect for individual rights and property. What’s the use of freedom when you’re still poor and trapped on a strip of land while your colonizer sits just a few meters away, sipping martinis on land that once belonged to your family for generations? What’s the use of justice when it’s merely rhetorical and forces you to normalize criminality of a much larger enduring scale? What’s the rule of law amidst the ruins of land? One could suggest that this is too much of an “all-in” project for our movement leaders and elected paragons of the democratic socialist conception. But truth be told, it is the Israelis, the Americans that support them, who’ve gone “all-in”. All in with the shuttering of Palestinian cultural life. All in with the death and mayhem of Palestinian villages and towns. All in with a genocide that’s been on full display now for nearly three horrific and unyielding years. Land back is a quite moderate demand when considering the true scale of violence and cruelty that the Zionists have bestowed upon the Palestinians, and now the Lebanese and Iranians. Isabella Hammad, a leading contemporary Palestinian novelist, had said , “My dream is that one day Palestine will no longer be a cause, it will just be a place, where some of us happen to be from, and we could fly into the airport without being interrogated and drive over to Nablus for lunch and then go further up to Akka and swim in the sea . . .” Palestine awaits us in joining completely in her moral and political imperative to restore the land, and in that process, restore humanity.
